source.title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Results and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Let S^{m-1} = {x in R^m : x_i >= 0, sum_i x_i = 1}. A Volterra quadratic stochastic operator on S^{m-1} has the form x'_k = x_k (1 + sum_i a_{ki} x_i), where A = (a_{ij}) is skew-symmetric and |a_{ki}| <= 1. Besides the Lyapunov functions already listed in Theorem 1, do there exist other kinds of Lyapunov functions for such Volterra QSOs?

evidence.quote: In paper [10] the general form of Volterra QSO ... is given x'_k = x_k (1 + sum_i a_ki x_i), k in E ... Moreover a_ki = -a_ik and |a_ki| <= 1.

Theorem 1. ... For the Volterra QSO (7) ... there exists a Lyapunov function ... There are Lyapunov functions of the form phi(x) = x_i/x_j ... Problem 1. Does there exist another kind of Lyapunov function for QSO (7)?

accepted.question_text: For a general quadratic stochastic operator V on the simplex S^{m-1}, define an appropriate notion of transversality extending the Volterra case, and determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the heredity tensor P = (P_{ij,k}) under which the operator is transversal.

evidence.quote: A skew-symmetric matrix A is called transversal if all even order leading (principal) minors are nonzero. A Volterra QSO V is called transversal if the corresponding skew-symmetric matrix A is transversal.
Problem 2. Define concept of transversality for arbitrary QSO and find necessary and sufficient condition on matrix P = (Pij,k) of a QSO under which the QSO is a transversal.

accepted.question_text: For a transversal Volterra quadratic stochastic operator, the trajectory spends asymptotically almost all of its time near the finite set X of fixed points, and one can record the successive visited neighborhoods by an itinerary n_1, n_2, .... Does there exist a trajectory whose itinerary is periodic?

evidence.quote: Then it is known that lim_{n->infinity} n_U / n = 1 i.e. the trajectory a despondent part of the time will stay in the neighborhood of the fixed points.

The sequence n1, n2, ... is called the itinerary (route-march) of the trajectory ... Since the set of fixed points is a finite set, the numbers n1, n2, ... will repeat. Problem 3. Is there a trajectory with periodic itinerary?

accepted.question_text: Consider the Volterra quadratic stochastic operator on S^2 given by x' = x(1 + a y - b z), y' = y(1 - a x + c z), z' = z(1 + b x - c y), where a, b, c are in [-1,1]. Theorem 3 states that if a, b, and c are all nonzero and have the same sign, then the ergodic theorem fails for this operator. Is that condition the right criterion for deciding when the ergodic theorem holds for this family?

evidence.quote: V : S^2 -> S^2, x' = x (1 + ay - bz), y' = y (1 - ax + cz), z' = z (1 + bx - cy), where a, b, c in [-1, 1].

Theorem 3. [3] If the parameters a, b, c for the Volterra QSO (9) have the same sign and each is non-zero, then the ergodic theorem will fail for this operator. Problem 4. Is the condition of Theorem 3 sufficient for the ergodic theorem to hold?

accepted.question_text: For a Volterra quadratic stochastic operator on S^{m-1} determined by a skew-symmetric matrix A, find necessary and sufficient conditions on A under which the ergodic theorem is true.

evidence.quote: In paper [10] the general form of Volterra QSO ... is given x'_k = x_k (1 + sum_i a_ki x_i), k in E ...
Problem 5. Find necessary and sufficient conditions on matrix A of Volterra QSO under which the ergodic theorem is true for the Volterra QSO on S^{m-1}, m >= 2.

accepted.question_text: Let V be a Volterra quadratic stochastic operator on S^{m-1}, let tau be a permutation of {1, ..., m}, and define the associated automorphism V_tau by x'_{tau(j)} = x_j (1 + sum_k a_{jk} x_k). Investigate the asymptotic behavior of trajectories of V_tau for an arbitrary permutation tau.

evidence.quote: Define QSO V_tau by V_tau : x'_{tau(j)} = x_j (1 + sum_k a_jk x_k), j = 1, ..., m ... Note that QSO V_tau is a non-Volterra QSO iff tau != id.
Problem 6. Investigate the asymptotic behavior of the trajectories of the operators V_tau (automorphisms) for an arbitrary permutation tau.

accepted.question_text: Fix l in {1, ..., m}. An l-Volterra quadratic stochastic operator is a QSO whose heredity coefficients satisfy P_{ij,k} = 0 whenever k is one of 1, ..., l and k is not in {i,j}, together with the positivity condition (11a) for k in {l+1, ..., m}. For a given l-Volterra QSO, determine the full set of its periodic trajectories.

evidence.quote: Fix l in E and assume that elements Pij,k of the matrix P satisfy Pij,k = 0 if k not in {i, j} for any k in {1, ..., l}, i, j in E; Pij,k > 0 ... if k in {l + 1, ..., m}. Definition 2. ... is called l-Volterra QSO.
Problem 7. Find the set of all periodic trajectories of a given l-Volterra QSO.

accepted.question_text: Develop a general dynamical theory for l-Volterra quadratic stochastic operators, including descriptions of their Lyapunov functions and the sets of limit points of their trajectories.

evidence.quote: Definition 2. For any fixed l in E, the QSO defined by (4), (5), (11) and (11a) is called l-Volterra QSO.
Problem 8. Develop theory of dynamical systems generated by a l-Volterra QSO. Find its Lyapunov functions, the set of limit points of its trajectories etc.

accepted.question_text: Given two quadratic stochastic operators V_1 and V_2, study how the dynamical properties of the convex combination V_lambda = lambda V_1 + (1 - lambda) V_2, with lambda in [0,1], are related to the properties of V_1 and V_2.

evidence.quote: In [15] it was considered the following family of QSOs V_lambda : S^2 -> S^2 : V_lambda = lambda V_0 + (1 - lambda) V_1, 0 <= lambda <= 1, where V_0 ... is a Volterra QSO and V_1 ... is a non-Volterra one.
Problem 9. For arbitrary two QSOs V1 and V2 connect the properties of V_lambda = lambda V1 + (1 - lambda)V2, lambda in [0, 1] with properties of V1 and V2.

accepted.question_text: Let E = E_1 union ... union E_q be a partition, and consider a xi-QSO defined by the condition P_{ij,k} = 0 whenever i and j belong to the same block E_p. Is there an analogue of Theorem 5 for every such xi-QSO, analogous to the F-QSO result asserting a unique fixed point with global exponential convergence?

evidence.quote: Theorem 5. [39] Any F-QSO has a unique fixed point (1, 0, ..., 0) ... for any x0 in S^m, the trajectory {x^(n)} tends to this fixed point exponentially rapidly.
Problem 10. Consider a partition xi = {E1, ..., Eq} of E ... Assume Pij,k = 0 if i, j in Ep ... Call the corresponding operator a xi-QSO. Is an analogue of Theorem 5 true for any xi-QSO?

accepted.question_text: Strictly non-Volterra quadratic stochastic operators satisfy P_{ij,k} = 0 whenever k belongs to {i,j}. For m = 3, Theorem 6 says that the operator (14) has a unique non-attractive fixed point and may have 2-cycles and 3-cycles depending on parameters. Does this theorem remain true for dimensions m >= 4?

evidence.quote: These QSOs satisfy Pij,k = 0 if k in {i, j}, for all i, j, k in E. Such an operator is called strictly non-Volterra QSO.

Theorem 6. [40] 1) For any values of parameters ... the operator (14) has a unique fixed point. Moreover the fixed point is not attractive. 2) The QSO (14) has 2-cycles and 3-cycles depending on the parameters (15). Problem 11. Is Theorem 6 true for m >= 4?

accepted.question_text: For each m, let alpha_m be the smallest constant such that every quadratic stochastic operator with all heredity coefficients P_{ij,k} > alpha_m is regular. Theorem 7 gives the bound P_{ij,k} > 1/(2m) and the exact value alpha_2 = (3 - sqrt(7))/2. Determine the exact values of alpha_m for all m >= 3.

evidence.quote: Theorem 7. [17] 1) If Pij,k > 1/(2m) then V is regular. 2) alpha_2 = 1/2 (3 - sqrt(7)).
Problem 12. Find exact values of alpha_m for any m >= 3.

accepted.question_text: A continuous operator V on S^{m-1} is called bistochastic if V(x) is majorized by x for every x in S^{m-1}. Investigate the behavior of trajectories of bistochastic quadratic stochastic operators.

evidence.quote: Definition 4. An arbitrary continuous operator V : S^{m-1} -> S^{m-1} satisfying the condition V(x) ≺ x, x in S^{m-1} is called a bistochastic operator.
Problem 13. Investigate the behavior of trajectories of the bistochastic quadratic operators.

accepted.question_text: Describe the set of all surjective quadratic stochastic operators defined on S^{m-1} for every dimension m >= 5.

evidence.quote: In [5] and [28] a description of surjective QSOs defined on S^{m-1} for m = 2, 3, 4 ... are given.
Problem 14. Describe the set of all surjective QSOs defined on S^{m-1} for any m >= 5.

accepted.question_text: Consider the construction of a quadratic stochastic operator from a finite graph G, a finite allele set Phi, and a strictly positive probability measure mu on the configuration space Omega, with heredity coefficients defined by formula (17) and the resulting operator by formula (18). Which quadratic stochastic operators arise from this construction?

evidence.quote: The QSO V acting on the simplex S(L, Phi) and determined by coefficients (17) is defined as follows ... l'(sigma) = sum_{sigma1,sigma2 in Omega} P_{sigma1 sigma2, sigma} l(sigma1) l(sigma2) (18).
Problem 15. Describe the class of QSOs which can be obtained by the construction.

accepted.question_text: When a quadratic stochastic operator is generated by a Gibbs measure associated with a Hamiltonian H and temperature T > 0, phase transitions can occur because the Gibbs measure may be non-unique. How do the thermodynamic features of the system, especially phase transitions, affect the behavior of trajectories of the corresponding QSO?

evidence.quote: More precisely, if E is continual set then one can associate the Gibbs measure mu by a Hamiltonian H ... and temperature T > 0 ... depending on the Hamiltonian and the values of the temperature the measure mu can be non unique. In this case there is a phase transition of the physical system with the Hamiltonian H.
Problem 16. (by N.N.Ganikhodjaev) How the thermodynamics (the phase transition) will effect to behavior of the trajectories of a QSO corresponding to a Gibbs measure of the Hamiltonian H?

accepted.question_text: Characterize all non-Volterra quadratic stochastic operators that can be reduced to several separate Volterra quadratic stochastic operators.

evidence.quote: Theorem 11. [38] The QSO constructed by the construction (18) with respect to measure (19) is reducible to q separate Volterra QSOs.
Problem 17. Describe the set of all non-Volterra QSOs which are reducible to several Volterra QSOs.

accepted.question_text: Find a probability measure mu different from the product form mu(sigma) = product_i mu_i(sigma_i) such that the associated non-Volterra quadratic stochastic operator can still be analyzed within the framework of the known theory of quadratic stochastic operators.

evidence.quote: Consider probability measure mu on Omega = Omega_1 x ... x Omega_q defined by mu(sigma) = product_{i=1}^q mu_i(sigma_i).
Problem 18. Find a measure mu different from (19) such that the non-Volterra QSO corresponding to mu can be investigated in the framework of a well known theory of QSOs.

accepted.question_text: Find a class of quadratic stochastic operators for which the set of initial states whose trajectories have historic behavior has positive Lebesgue measure, where historic behavior means that for some continuous function f the time averages (1/(n+1)) sum_{i=0}^n f(V^i(x)) fail to converge.

evidence.quote: We say that a trajectory {x, V(x), V^2(x), ...} has historic behavior if for some continuous function f : S^{m-1} -> R the average lim_{n->infinity} 1/(n + 1) sum_{i=0}^n f(V^i(x)) does not exist.
Problem 19. Find a class of QSOs such that the set of initial states which give rise to trajectories with historic behavior has positive Lebesque measure.

accepted.question_text: Study the theory of quadratic stochastic operators whose heredity coefficients factor as P_{ij,k} = a_{ik} b_{jk}, so that the operator has the form (V(x))_k = (A(x))_k (B(x))_k. In particular, develop the general dynamical theory of operators defined by formula (21).

evidence.quote: Consider QSO (4), (5) with additional condition Pij,k = a_ik b_jk ... Then the QSO V corresponding to the coefficients (20) has the form x'_k = (V(x))_k = (A(x))_k · (B(x))_k, (21).
Problem 20. Develop theory of QSOs defined by (21).

accepted.question_text: Describe all quadratic stochastic operators V on S^{m-1} for which there exists an integer r >= 2 such that V^r(x) = V(x) for every x in S^{m-1}.

evidence.quote: QSO V is a Bernstein mapping if V^2 = V ... The problem is to describe all Bernstein mappings explicitly.
Problem 21. Describe all QSOs which satisfy V^r(x) = V(x) for any x in S^{m-1} and some r >= 2.

accepted.question_text: For topological conjugacy classes of quadratic stochastic operators, does there exist a finite complete system of indicator polynomials, and if so, what is a basis of the system of indicators?

evidence.quote: Definition 6. A polynomial f(Pij,k) is called an indicator ... Definition 7. A system f1, ..., ft of indicators is called complete ... A minimal complete system of indicators is called a basis.
Problem 22. Does there exist a finite complete system of indicators? Find the basis of the system of indicators.
